title: Removing low-influence directions from convex sets
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: Does there exist a function \(\tau :(0,1)\to [0,1]\) with \(\lim _{\varepsilon \to 0^{+}}\tau (\varepsilon )=0\) such that the following holds for every \(n\ge 1\), every centrally symmetric convex Borel set \(K\subseteq \mathbb{R} ^{n}\), every unit vector v and every \(\varepsilon \in (0,1)\)? If \(Inf_{v}[K]\le \varepsilon\), then there exists a centrally symmetric convex Borel set \(C\subseteq v\perp\) such that \(\gamma _{n}(K \triangle  (C+\mathbb{R} v))\le \tau (\varepsilon )\). The same \(\tau\) must work in all dimensions and for all such sets and directions.
context:
The approximating set is unrestricted along v. Moving any distance parallel to v cannot change membership, although membership may depend arbitrarily on the orthogonal projection.

The definition compares membership with the squared coordinate in direction v. It differs from boundary surface area, resampling influence and the total influence summed over directions.

Proposition 11 says that zero influence is equivalent, up to Gaussian null sets, to membership being independent of the coordinate along v. The conjecture asks for a dimension-free robust form of that statement.

Conjecture 1 controls the number of relevant directions using total influence. This card is Conjecture 2: one specified direction has small influence, and only that direction must be removed.
why: Would make convex influence a robust measure of whether a Gaussian direction matters, strengthening the analogy between symmetric convex sets and Boolean functions with irrelevant variables.

sentences: The problem concerns symmetric convex sets under standard Gaussian measure.
A specified direction has small convex influence, measured by a normalized second-moment statistic.
The conjecture asks whether the set is close to a symmetric convex cylinder that ignores this direction.
The approximation error must tend to zero with influence independently of dimension.
The exact zero-influence case is known, while the robust dimension-free statement remains the source’s Conjecture 2.

definitions: \(\gamma _{n}\) is standard Gaussian probability measure, the law of X with independent \(N(0,1)\) coordinates. Central symmetry means \(K=- K\), with symmetry about the origin. Convexity means \(tx+(1- t)y\in K\) for \(x,y\in K\) and \(t\in [0,1]\). Write \(1_{K}\) for the indicator of K. The convex influence in a Euclidean unit direction v is \(Inf_{v}[K]=(1/\sqrt{2}) E[1_{K}(X)(1- \langle v,X\rangle ^{2})]\). This is nonnegative for centrally symmetric convex K. The orthogonal subspace is \(v\perp =\{y:\langle v,y\rangle =0\}\), and \(C+\mathbb{R} v=\{y+tv:y\in C,t\in \mathbb{R}\}\) is a cylinder whose membership depends only on the projection \(x- \langle v,x\rangle v\). The symmetric difference \(K\triangle \mathrm{L}\) consists of points in exactly one of K and L, so its Gaussian measure is the probability that their membership indicators disagree. Empty sets and the whole space are permitted. No lower or upper bound away from zero or one is imposed on \(\gamma _{n}(K)\), and no bound on total influence is assumed.
answer_criterion: Prove a single modulus \(\tau\) tending to zero that bounds the Gaussian approximation error uniformly over the stated sets, dimensions and directions, or prove that no such modulus exists. Equivalently for a negative answer, exhibit a sequence with directional influence tending to zero while its Gaussian distance from every symmetric convex cylinder in that direction stays bounded below by a positive constant. A dimension-dependent modulus or a cylinder in some other direction does not suffice.
